tests.name: conversions
tests.description: Literals and conversions. The literal syntax of every type: Boolean, String with its escapes and the backslash before a non-escape character, Integer (the minus sign being the unary operator), Decimal (no exponent), Date, Time and DateTime with partial precision, the T suffix and timezone offsets, Quantity with UCUM units and the calendar duration keywords singular and plural, the empty collection, and literals the pinned grammar refuses (double quotes, an unterminated string, exponents, a missing year, an offset on a Time, an unknown or capitalised keyword). The implicit conversions of the Conversion table (Integer to Decimal, Integer and Decimal to Quantity with unit '1', Date to DateTime) and their absence where the table has none. The conversion functions toBoolean, toInteger, toLong (3.0.0, STU), toDecimal, toQuantity with and without a unit (a calendar duration keyword as the unit and the calendar conversion factors included), toString, toDate and toDateTime (with 3.0.0's format argument, STU), toTime and every convertsToX: what converts, what each conversion yields, what does not convert (empty for toX, false for convertsToX), more than one input item (error) and an empty input (empty); and FHIR primitives and FHIR Quantity converted as the System types the R4 and R5 pages map them to. Where 2.0.0 and 3.0.0 differ the case follows 2.0.0, except where 3.0.0 fixes a defect of 2.0.0 (toQuantity(unit) returning a Boolean, toString returning false, the doubled backslash of the sign in the integer and decimal regexes) or defines what 2.0.0 does not (toLong, the unit '1' of a unitless quantity string, toDate of a DateTime without timezone normalisation, the format argument, the unary minus on a String). Left out because the text does not settle them: Long literals (the pinned grammar has no L suffix), integer literals and integer strings outside the Integer range, decimals beyond the stated range and precision, fractional seconds beyond milliseconds, date and time literals and strings with an impossible component (month 13, 30 February, hour 25) and whether the failure is a parse or a run-time error, week and ordinal dates, a quantity literal whose unit is not valid UCUM, a time string with an offset, a date-only string given to toDateTime (such as '2015-02-04', with no T at all) or a datetime string ending in T, the timezone offset and the precision of a toDateTime(format) result when the template has no Z code and stops before the seconds, a quantity string whose unquoted word is not a calendar keyword or is capitalised, the trailing zeros and the number of fraction digits toString writes for a Decimal, how toString writes the value of a quantity from an integer literal, a Z offset and a DateTime that ends at the year with T, the unit spelling 3.0.0 uses for a calendar quantity in toString, conversions between different units without UCUM support, convertsToQuantity with a unit commensurable with the input's but different from it (true where the implementation converts, false where it may not), the FHIR integer64 and time primitives (no suite input holds one), convertsToQuantity and toDate with an empty argument beyond the general rule, a unit or format argument that is not a String, toInteger of a Long outside the Integer range, convertsToLong of a string outside 64 bits, and the format codes 3.0.0 makes optional. iif, and the operators already covered by the math and equality-comparison areas, are not repeated.

group.name: REQ-CONVERSIONS-004
group.description: A backslash before a character that starts no escape sequence is dropped, as the text's examples show (\/ is not in the table, so it is such a sequence)
group.source: No other escape sequences besides those listed above are recognized.
If a `\` is used at the beginning of a non-escape sequence, it will be ignored and will not appear in the sequence.
define TestEscape1: '\p' // 'p'
define TestEscape2: '\\p' // '\p'
define TestEscape3: '\3' // '3'
define TestEscape4: '\u005' // 'u005'
define TestEscape5: '\' // ''
'\u005' // 'u005' ; unicode escape sequences have 4 characters, not 3, hence not detected as an escaped sequence
'\' // '' ; an empty string

group.name: REQ-CONVERSIONS-005
group.description: An Integer literal is a sequence of digits; the minus sign is the unary operator, applied after invocation, so a negative literal must be parenthesised before a function call
group.source: The `Integer` type represents whole numbers in the range -2^31^ to 2^31^-1.
Note that the minus sign (`-`) in the representation of a negative integer is not part of the literal, it is the unary negation operator defined as part of FHIRPath syntax.
Note that the minus sign (`-`) in the representation of a negative integer is not part of the literal, it is the unary negation operator defined as part of FHIRPath syntax.
|Sequences of digits in the range 0..2^32^-1
Integer: 0, 45

Because the invocation operator (`.`) has a higher precedence than the unary negation (`-`), the unary negation will be applied to the result of the combine of 7 and 3, resulting in an error (because unary negation cannot be applied to a list):
-(7.combine(3)) // ERROR
The unary operators support a single item input operand of type Integer, Long, Decimal, or Quantity.
Using with any incompatible type will end and signal an error to the calling environment.

group.name: REQ-CONVERSIONS-006
group.description: A Decimal literal is digits, a point and digits, with at least the 10^-8 step; exponential notation and a point without digits on either side do not parse
group.source: The `Decimal` type represents real values in the range (-10^28^+1)/10^8^ to (10^28^-1)/10^8^ with a step size of 10^-8^.
Implementations can provide support for larger decimals and higher precision, but must provide at least the range and precision defined here.
Decimal literals cannot use exponential notation.
Decimal literals cannot use exponential notation.
|Sequences of digits with a decimal point, in the range (-10^28^+1)/10^8^..(10^28^-1)/10^8^
Note: If there are discrepancies between this documentation and the grammar included at the above link, the grammar is considered the source of truth.

group.name: REQ-CONVERSIONS-007
group.description: A Date literal is @ and YYYY-MM-DD, month and day optional; the year must be present
group.source: A date literal begins with an `@`
It uses the format **YYYY-MM-DD** format, though month and day parts are optional, and a separator is required between provided components
Years must be present (e.g. `@-10-20` is not a valid Date in FHIRPath)

group.name: REQ-CONVERSIONS-008
group.description: A Time literal is @T and hh:mm:ss.fff, partial from the hour; it has no timezone offset, and one written after it does not parse (the grammar, the source of truth, overrides the Lexical Elements table that shows an offset)
group.source: A time begins with a `@T`
It uses the **Thh:mm:ss.fff** format
Time values in FHIRPath do not have a timezone or timezone offset.
Time values in FHIRPath do not have a timezone or timezone offset.
Time: @T14:34:28 (@ followed by ISO8601 compliant time beginning with T, no timezone offset)

Note: If there are discrepancies between this documentation and the grammar included at the above link, the grammar is considered the source of truth.

group.name: REQ-CONVERSIONS-009
group.description: A DateTime literal is a date, T and a time with an optional offset in which Z means +00:00; a T after a year, year-month or full date makes a partial DateTime, not a Date
group.source: A datetime literal begins with an `@`
It uses the **YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ss.fff(+|-)hh:mm** format
**Z** is allowed as a synonym for the zero (+00:00) UTC offset.
A `T` can be used at the end of any date (year, year-month, or year-month-day) to indicate a partial DateTime.

The suffix `T` is allowed after a year, year-month, or year-month-day literal because without it, there would be no way to specify a partial DateTime with only a year, month, or day; the literal would always result in a Date value.
@2014-01-25T14:30:14.559Z // A date time with UTC timezone offset
@2014-01-25T14:30 // A partial DateTime with year, month, day, hour, and minute
@2014-03-25T // A partial DateTime with year, month, and day
@2014-01T // A partial DateTime with year and month
@2014T // A partial DateTime with only the year
DateTime: @2015-02-04T14:34:28+09:00 (@ followed by ISO8601 compliant date/time)
** `DateTime`: must be exactly the same, respecting the timezone offset (though +00:00 = -00:00 = Z)

group.name: REQ-CONVERSIONS-010
group.description: An offset must have hours and minutes; +09 after a DateTime is no offset but the addition of the Integer 9, which date/time arithmetic refuses
group.source: Timezone offset is optional, but if present the notation **(+|-)hh:mm** is used (so must include both minutes and hours)
Timezone offset is optional, but if present the notation `(+|-)hh:mm`{:.formatted} is used (so must include both minutes and hours)
The left operand must be a `Date`, `DateTime`, or `Time` value, and the right operand must be a `Quantity` with a time-valued unit
If there is more than one item, or an item of an incompatible type, the evaluation of the expression will end and signal an error to the calling environment.

group.name: REQ-CONVERSIONS-011
group.description: A Quantity literal is a number followed by a quoted UCUM unit or a calendar duration keyword, an integer value becoming a Decimal
group.source: The `Quantity` literal is a number (integer or decimal), followed by a (single-quoted) string representing a valid Unified Code for Units of Measure <<UCUM>> unit or calendar duration keyword. If the value literal is an Integer, it will be implicitly converted to a Decimal in the resulting Quantity value:
Quantity: 10 'mg', 4 days
2 years // Calendar units
Implementations shall support comparison and arithmetic operations on quantities with units where the units are the same.
** `Decimal`: values must be equal, trailing zeroes after the decimal are ignored

group.name: REQ-CONVERSIONS-012
group.description: Every calendar duration keyword is accepted singular and plural, and both spell the same unit
group.source: The `Quantity` type represents quantities with a specified unit, where the `value` component is defined as a `Decimal`, and the `unit` element is represented as a `String` that is required to be either a valid Unified Code for Units of Measure <<UCUM>> unit or one of the calendar duration keywords, singular or plural.
|`year`/`years` |`'year'` |`~ 1 'a'`
|`month`/`months` |`'month'` |`~ 1 'mo'`
|`week`/`weeks` |`'week'` |`~ 1 'wk'`
|`hour`/`hours` |`'hour'` |`~ 1 'h'`
|`minute`/`minutes` |`'minute'` |`~ 1 'min'`
|`second`/`seconds` |`'second'` |`= 1 's'`
|`millisecond`/`milliseconds` |`'millisecond'` |`= 1 'ms'`
Implementations shall support comparison and arithmetic operations on quantities with units where the units are the same.

group.source: If the `unit` argument is provided, it must be the string representation of a UCUM code (or a FHIRPath calendar duration keyword).
If the `unit` argument is provided and the input can be [**converted**](#unit-conversions), the result is the converted quantity, otherwise the result is empty.

If the input quantity can be converted, the result is true, otherwise, the result is false.
Implementations are not required to support a complete UCUM implementation, and may return empty (`{ }`) when the `unit` argument is used and it is different than the input quantity unit.

The evaluation will end and signal an error to the calling environment
